With over 550 patients enrolled, the initial data readout for the DME program in both studies is expected early in the fourth quarter of 2027.

Topline data from the LUGANO and LUCIA trials for DURAVYU in wet AMD were announced in August 2026 and October 2026, respectively, where the primary endpoint of statistical non-inferiority in mean change in best corrected visual acuity (BCVA) versus on-label 2 mg aflibercept control was not achieved despite visual acuity improvements for a majority of patients treated with DURAVYU.

• On October 19, 2026, we announced topline results from LUCIA, the second pivotal Phase 3 clinical trial of DURAVYU for the potential treatment of wet AMD. o In LUCIA, despite demonstrating visual improvement, DURAVYU did not achieve the primary endpoint of statistical non-inferiority in mean change in best corrected visual acuity (BCVA) versus on-label 2 mg aflibercept control. o DURAVYU achieved key secondary endpoints including a continued favorable safety profile with redosing, along with a meaningful reduction in treatment burden, durability as demonstrated by supplement-free rates, and strong anatomic control at Week 56, consistent with the first Phase 3 LUGANO clinical trial. o In a pooled analysis of the greater than 50% of patients in both trials who were supplement-free up to Week 56, DURAVYU was observed to be statistically non-inferior in mean change in BCVA versus on-label 2 mg aflibercept control. o We will conclude the wet AMD program before completion of the full second year of the Phase 3 studies for both LUGANO and LUCIA, while also allowing additional patients to complete year two to support the necessary safety database for a potential new drug application for DME. o We will complete additional analyses of both the LUGANO and LUCIA data along with the pooled Phase 3 datasets to further assess next steps for DURAVYU as a potential treatment for wet AMD.

• In October 2026, following review of topline results from LUCIA, the second pivotal Phase 3 clinical trial evaluating DURAVYU™ for the treatment of wet AMD, the Board of Directors approved a strategic prioritization plan (the “Prioritization”) designed to reduce operating expenses and focus resources on the Phase 3 program for DURAVYU™ in DME.

R&D Updates • On August 17, 2026, we announced topline data for LUGANO, our first pivotal Phase 3 clinical trial evaluating DURAVYU for wet AMD. o Despite demonstrating visual acuity improvements for a majority of patients, LUGANO did not meet the primary endpoint in its full dataset; an ad hoc analysis excluding nine DURAVYU patients with ≥15-letter vision loss due to non-wet AMD etiologies demonstrated non-inferiority versus aflibercept (nominal p=0.0096). o LUGANO demonstrated clinically meaningful results that reinforce DURAVYU’s potential to improve the treatment paradigm in wet AMD, with compelling key secondary endpoints, including reduction in treatment burden, supplement-free rates, favorable safety profile with redosing, and strong anatomic control through Week 56 compared to on-label aflibercept.
Topline data for both DME trials are anticipated early in the fourth quarter of 2027.
